issues.description: The script uses XMLHttpRequest to fetch arbitrary code and executes it via a[a][a](x.responseText), which is equivalent to eval(). This is a remote code execution vulnerability.
issues.recommendation: Remove dynamic code execution or restrict to trusted, versioned sources. Avoid using eval or Function constructors.

issues.description: The script executes code from arbitrary URLs using a highly obfuscated pattern (a[a][a]), which is a sign of code obfuscation.
issues.recommendation: Avoid obfuscation and use clear, maintainable code. Remove dynamic code execution.

issues.description: The script can insert and execute arbitrary code into the DOM, which can lead to DOM-based XSS if user input or untrusted data is used.
issues.recommendation: Sanitize all inputs and avoid using innerHTML or similar methods with untrusted data.

issues.description: The script requests and executes third-party libraries via @require from GreasyFork and CDN, but does not pin versions with hashes, exposing to supply chain risks.
issues.recommendation: Pin all dependencies to specific versions and use trusted CDNs with integrity hashes.

issues.description: The script applies for high-privilege grants (unsafeWindow, GM_getTabs, GM_saveTab, etc.) that are not all used in the visible code, indicating possible permission overreach.
issues.recommendation: Request only the minimum permissions required for functionality.

issues.description: The script stores a unique user ID (UUID) in local storage via GM.setValue and increments a counter, which can be used for tracking.
issues.recommendation: Inform users about tracking and minimize persistent identifiers.

issues.description: The script's @antifeature explicitly states tracking for performance debugging.
issues.recommendation: Disclose all tracking in documentation and provide opt-out.

details: Unique user ID (UUID) stored and incremented for each use.

summary: This script poses severe security and privacy risks. It contains remote code execution via dynamic code loading and eval-like constructs, code obfuscation, DOM XSS risk, privacy-invasive tracking, excessive permissions, and supply chain risks. It should NOT be approved for use.
